correctness.rationale: Uniform k-two-cycle involutions are sampled by a uniformly chosen moved set r=2k and uniform perfect matching on it. For positions a<b, d=b−a, both moved contributes r²/[2n(n−1)] (direct partners always invert, others by exchangeability); mixed fixed/moved contributes r(n−r)(n−d−1)/[n(n−1)(n−2)], both fixed contributes zero. Substitution gives 2k²/[n(n−1)]+2k(n−2k)(n−d−1)/[n(n−1)(n−2)] for n≥3; n=2 is checked separately. Gap slope and k-monotonicity follow by endpoint convex interpolation. Coupling consecutive classes by pairing a uniformly selected pair of current fixed positions preserves uniformity because each (k+1)-cycle target has k+1 predecessors and each k source has C(n−2k,2) choices. Exact inversion increase is 1+2#{t between a,b whose pi(t) lies between}, so strictly positive for every transition and gives strict stochastic increasing h(I) and conditional covariances. Sum over gaps produces known mean k(2n−k)/3. Independent exact all-involution enumeration n=2..8 checked local probabilities.
